detail:
Schroth is a physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercise (PSSE) method built on 3D correction of the individual's curve pattern. It uses sensorimotor, postural, and corrective breathing exercises, with auto-correction — the patient actively correcting their own curve — as the core element.

A 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis by Ceballos-Laita et al. pooled 6 randomized controlled trials (144 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis). Short-term, Schroth improved the Cobb angle with a mean difference of −3.18°, along with quality of life and trunk rotation angle, compared with no intervention. However, the authors note the Cobb angle improvement "did not exceed the minimum clinically important difference" — reported plainly as the source states it.

The SOSORT 2016 guidelines recommend PSSE as a first step to prevent or limit curve progression during growth. The source material stresses that these programs must be designed by therapists specifically trained in the approach — they are not DIY exercises.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about whether scoliosis-specific exercises are appropriate for you.
sourceName: Systematic review and meta-analysis (Ceballos-Laita et al., 2023)
sourceVideoTitle: Effects of Schroth exercises on adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
